# Memory management


::: {.callout-tip icon=false} 
## :dart: Learning goals of this course
- Understand memory management
:::


## Why?

- Pointers give control over memory.
- Pass data to a different program part without copying it (`functions`, `classes`,...).
- Control when to delete data [dynamic]{style="color:orange;"}  vs. [static]{style="color:blue"} memory.

::: {.columns}
:::: {.column width="33%"}
```{dot}
//| echo: false
//| label: stack-heap
//| fig-width: 3
digraph memory {
  node [shape=plaintext, fontname="Courier"];
  mem [label=<
    <TABLE BORDER="0" CELLBORDER="1" CELLSPACING="0">
      <TR><TD HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110" PORT="cmd1"><FONT COLOR="blue"><I>stack</I></FONT></TD></TR>
      <TR><TD HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110" PORT="cmd2"><FONT COLOR="blue"><I>stack</I></FONT></TD></TR>
      <TR><TD HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110" PORT="cmd3"><FONT COLOR="blue"><I>stack</I></FONT></TD></TR>
      <TR><TD HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110" PORT="cmd4">...</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110" PORT="cmd5"><FONT COLOR="orange"><I>heap</I></FONT></TD></TR>
      <TR><TD HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110" PORT="cmd6"><FONT COLOR="orange"><I>heap</I></FONT></TD></TR>
    </TABLE>
  >];

  //mem:cmd2:e -> mem:cmd6:e;
}
```
::::

::::  {.column width="66%"} 
- [static]{style="color:blue"} memory managed by compiler ([stack]{style="color:blue"})
- [dynamic]{style="color:orange;"} memory managed by user ([heap]{style="color:orange;"})
- dynamic memory can be accessed with pointers (stored in stack)
- address space in heap is accessed with `new`
::::
:::

## An array in heap

```{dot}
//| echo: false
//| label: stack-heap
//| fig-width: 3
digraph memory {
  node [shape=plaintext, fontname="Courier"];
  mem [label=<
    <TABLE BORDER="0" CELLBORDER="1" CELLSPACING="0">
      <TR><TD HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110" PORT="cmd1">...</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110" PORT="cmd2">v[3]</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110" PORT="cmd3">v[2]</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110" PORT="cmd4">v[1]</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110" PORT="cmd5">v = v[0]</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110" PORT="cmd6">...</TD></TR>
    </TABLE>
  >];

}
```

- We store address of `v[0]` in `v`.
- Since ` v[1]`, $\ldots$ neighbour `v[0]` we also know their addresses.
- More about this when talking about pointer arithmetic.

## Multi-dimensional arrays

In the C/C++ standard there is no dynamic multi-dimensional array.

1. option: Use a pointer to a pointer.
   - Access via `a[i][j]`.
	 - Not very good memory layout on modern computer architectures (pointer chasing).
    
2. option: Use an one-dimensional array and do the index calculations by hand.
	 - Access via `a[i + j*n]`.

3. option: Use an external library that implements 2d arrays.
	 - Access is usually provided by `a(i, j)`

## Good practice!

Always delete storage you allocated with `new`. 


## Pointer arithmetics

- Arithmetics on pointers allowed.
- `d[i]` equivalent to `*(d + i)`

## Pointer arithmetics

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="33%"}
```{dot}
//| echo: false
//| label: ptr-arith1
//| fig-width: 3
digraph mem1 {
  node [shape=plaintext, fontname="Courier"];
  mem [label=<
    <TABLE BORDER="0" CELLBORDER="0" CELLSPACING="0">
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" SIDES="LR" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">...</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">v[3]</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">v[2]</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">v[1]</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">*v = v[0]</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" SIDES="LR" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">...</TD></TR>
    </TABLE>
  >];
}
```
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
```{dot}
//| echo: false
//| label: ptr-arith2
//| fig-width: 3
digraph mem2 {
  node [shape=plaintext, fontname="Courier"];
  mem [label=<
    <TABLE BORDER="0" CELLBORDER="0" CELLSPACING="0">
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" SIDES="LR" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">...</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">*(v+3)</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">*(v+2)</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">*(v+1)</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">*v = v[0]</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" SIDES="LR" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">...</TD></TR>
    </TABLE>
  >];
}
```
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
```{dot}
//| echo: false
//| label: ptr-arith3
//| fig-width: 3
digraph mem3 {
  node [shape=plaintext, fontname="Courier"];
  mem [label=<
    <TABLE BORDER="0" CELLBORDER="0" CELLSPACING="0">
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" SIDES="LR" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">...</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">(v+1)[2]</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">(v+1)[1]</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">(v+1)[0]</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">*v = v[0]</TD></TR>
      <TR><TD BORDER="1" SIDES="LR" HEIGHT="28" WIDTH="110">...</TD></TR>
    </TABLE>
  >];
}
```
:::
